draft.title: Market research practices
card: Market research is collecting and analysing data to learn what customers want. A business uses it to make better decisions.
Surveys
a set of questions given to many people, often online. They give answers from a large group that are easy to count.
Interviews
a one-on-one or small group conversation. They give detailed answers about why people think or choose as they do.
Observation
watching what customers actually do, such as which shelves they stop at. It shows behaviour rather than what people say. Data only helps once it is analysed for patterns.
draft.remember: Research gathers data from customers, then analysis turns it into answers.

a.q: Which research practice records what customers actually do, rather than what they say?
opts: Observation
Survey
Interview
Analysis
a.why: Observation means watching real behaviour. A survey and an interview both depend on what people choose to say, and analysis is the step after the data is collected.

b.q: Sam opens a gym in Geelong. He wants detailed reasons why local people have quit other gyms. Which practice suits this best?
opts: Interviews with people who have left a gym
An online survey with only tick-box answers
Counting cars in a rival gym's car park
Collecting data and then not analysing it
b.why: Interviews let people explain their reasons in detail. A tick-box survey reaches more people but gives little on why, and counting cars shows numbers only.
b.clue: Which practice gives detailed answers about why?

b.best: Interviews with people who have left a gym

problems.detail: The sentence 'Data only helps once it is analysed for patterns' sits inside the Observation bullet, so students may think analysis applies only to observation rather than to all research. It belongs in its own bullet or in the first bullet.

The distractor 'Collecting data and then not analysing it' is not a research practice and is plainly wrong, so the question is easier than it should be. A plausible practice, such as observation of gym users, would test the idea better.

check.summary: Facts and answers check out (a: Observation, b: Interviews). The analysis sentence is misplaced in the Observation bullet, and one distractor in question b is too obviously wrong.
